claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To assess this properly, I'll need to gather some information about you and the children involved.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you responsible for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 21 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I appreciate you providing the context.

Since Alex is 21 years old, I need to ask you an important question to determine his eligibility:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as university, college, or an apprenticeship)?**

Child Benefit can continue beyond age 16 for children under 20 who are in approved education or training, but it typically stops when they reach 20 unless they remain in that approved education or training. Since Alex is 21, I need to understand his current situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He actually works full-time at a local warehouse.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

I have one more question to complete the assessment:

**Does Alex work 24 hours or more per week in his full-time warehouse job?**

This is important because Child Benefit stops if a child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he does - he works full-time, so definitely more than 24 hours a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all the necessary information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Based on the information you've provided, let me explain the situation:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**You are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

1. **Age limit**: Child Benefit normally ends when a child turns 16. It can continue until age 20 only if they remain in approved education or training. Since Alex is 21, he has already exceeded this age limit.

2. **Full-time work**: Additionally, Child Benefit stops when a child starts paid work for 24 hours or more per week and is no longer in approved education or training. Alex works full-time at a warehouse, which exceeds the 24-hour threshold.

Since Alex meets both conditions for ineligibility (being over the age limit and working full-time without being in education or training), you cannot claim Child Benefit for him.

If you have any other children under 16, or children aged 16-19 in approved education or training, you may be able to claim Child Benefit for them instead. Would you like to provide information about any other children?
